svg.title: Four Checks Before a Recovery Submission
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-statutory-and-contract-preflight; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before a Recovery Submission; subtitle: Each failed check routes to remediation or a declined claim; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Apply every relevant branch to the engagement; branches describe operating checks, not a probability model. Federal tax fee rules, state representation rules, and private carrier terms address different obligations.; caption: Submit only after authority, contractual eligibility, tax scope, and jurisdictional credentials are resolved. Preserve the evidence supporting each decision.; stages: label: Authority and permitted information use; value: Proceed with documented authority and valid access; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Require signed authority, baseline invoice snapshots, and least-privilege access. Where tax-return preparer information rules apply, evaluate 26 U.S.C. 7216 and 26 CFR 301.7216-3; a generic Letter of Authorization does not replace any required disclosure or use consent. Otherwise obtain missing permissions first.; label: Carrier and vendor recovery entitlement; value: Proceed only for eligible timely claims; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Inspect actual carrier guarantee waivers, service exclusions, filing deadlines, prior credits, and authorized API use. For utilities, retain the controlling tariff and effective date. If entitlement fails, remove the claim rather than bypassing a carrier restriction or manufacturing a billing error.; label: Federal tax scope and substantiation; value: Proceed with supported eligibility and permitted fees; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Have a qualified practitioner assess 31 CFR 10.27 as applicable to the specific service, including exceptions and relevant judicial limitations. For WOTC, verify 26 U.S.C. 51(c)(4) hire-date coverage and 51(d)(13) certification requirements; where prescreening applies, complete it by the offer date and submit within 28 days after work begins.; label: State credentials and appeal calendar; value: Proceed through properly credentialed representation; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Check state property-tax consultant rules, permissible fee terms, and local appeal procedures. In Texas, review Occupations Code Chapter 1152 and Tax Code 41.44, including applicable exceptions and actual notice dates. If credentials or deadlines fail, refer appropriately or decline the affected matter.

rect.title: label: Authority and permitted information use; value: Proceed with documented authority and valid access; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Require signed authority, baseline invoice snapshots, and least-privilege access. Where tax-return preparer information rules apply, evaluate 26 U.S.C. 7216 and 26 CFR 301.7216-3; a generic Letter of Authorization does not replace any required disclosure or use consent. Otherwise obtain missing permissions first.

rect.title: label: Carrier and vendor recovery entitlement; value: Proceed only for eligible timely claims; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Inspect actual carrier guarantee waivers, service exclusions, filing deadlines, prior credits, and authorized API use. For utilities, retain the controlling tariff and effective date. If entitlement fails, remove the claim rather than bypassing a carrier restriction or manufacturing a billing error.
